$schema_note: Aether environment-variable inventory, including variables without CLI flags and hidden/internal variables.
precedence: CLI flag (set_var overwrite) > pre-set env var > compiled default; RUST_LOG overrides AETHER_LOG_LEVEL; interactive prompts appear only for protocol/scan/ip when neither flag nor env is set.
one_to_one_note: The flag<->env mapping is NOT always 1:1: --no-data-check/--validate-secs/--reconnect-secs each map to TWO variables; --tor/--tor-reverse/--tor-only share ONE variable; --psiphon* share one variable; AETHER_TOR_BRIDGES encodes auto/off/lines; AETHER_WIW_PEERS/AETHER_MIM_PEERS encode 'auto' (scan) or endpoints; 20 documented variables and 3 hidden variables have no flag; AETHER_TEAM_ENDPOINT is set by the core itself.

variables.name: AETHER_SOCKS
variables.effect: local SOCKS5 listener address; NO authentication is enforced; non-loopback binds log a security warning
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L581; lib.rs L120-123; socks.rs serve()
variables.notes: Listener is bound BEFORE tunnel establishment and held (unanswered) between tunnel reconnects. Bind 127.0.0.1 for same-device zeptun.

variables.name: AETHER_HTTP_PROXY
variables.effect: also expose an HTTP CONNECT proxy on this address

variables.name: AETHER_UPSTREAM
variables.accepted_values: socks5://[user:pass@]host:port | http://... | https://... | bare host:port (=socks5); %-encode passwords containing @ or :
variables.effect: dial everything (tunnel, scan, WARP API, ECH lookup) through an upstream proxy; SOCKS5-with-UDP-ASSOCIATE upstream carries every transport; HTTP CONNECT only the h2 carrier
variables.notes: Aether contains a full SOCKS5 client incl. UDP ASSOCIATE for upstream detours (upstream.rs L610-702).

variables.name: AETHER_MARK
variables.effect: SO_MARK firewall mark on every outbound socket (QUIC, WireGuard, scan, upstream, route-direct, WARP API, DoH); startup fails if the mark cannot be set rather than send unmarked traffic
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L612; egress.rs L16-78; DOCS.en.md 'Firewall mark'
variables.notes: Built for tun front ends (hev-socks5-tunnel, tun2socks, zeptun). Pair with `ip rule add fwmark 0xff lookup main priority 100` (priority must sort BEFORE zeptun's rule range 9000-9009). With --mark and no --upstream the WARP API needs an IP address (--api-address).

variables.name: AETHER_EXIT_LOC
variables.effect: refuse a tunnel whose exit country is unwanted; checked through the finished tunnel before SOCKS5 serves, then periodically

variables.name: AETHER_EXIT_LOC_SECS
variables.effect: exit-country recheck interval

variables.name: AETHER_STATS
variables.effect: periodically log up/down volume and tunnel uptime

variables.name: AETHER_STATS_SECS
variables.effect: stats log interval

variables.name: AETHER_QUICK_RECONNECT
variables.default: off (asks interactively when a last-connection file exists)
variables.effect: auto-accept reconnecting with the last known working gateway

variables.name: AETHER_IP
variables.effect: scan/connect address family: IPv4 only (default)
variables.notes: Sets AETHER_IP=v4 | Sets AETHER_IP=v6 | Sets AETHER_IP=both | DOCS.en.md env table spells the values '4, 6, dual' - both spellings accepted; source help is authoritative: v4|v6|both.

variables.name: AETHER_PEER
variables.effect: force a MASQUE (or WireGuard, for wg/gool-outer) peer, skip scanning
variables.notes: For WireGuard/WarpInWarp AETHER_WG_PEER wins over AETHER_PEER (lib.rs L1236-1238, L2449-2451). Setting AETHER_PEER alone selects Protocol::Masque (lib.rs L156-160).

variables.name: AETHER_WG_PEER
variables.effect: force the WireGuard peer (warp-in-warp outer), skip scanning

variables.name: AETHER_WIW_OUTER_PEER
variables.effect: pin the outer hop of classic gool (WARP-in-WARP); naming one hop selects classic gool

variables.name: AETHER_WIW_INNER_PEER
variables.effect: pin the inner hop of classic gool

variables.name: AETHER_WIW_PEERS
variables.effect: both classic-gool hops in one value (or only the outer)

variables.name: AETHER_WIW_PEERS=auto
variables.effect: scan for both classic-gool hops, ignoring endpoints left in the environment

variables.name: AETHER_PROTOCOL=masque
variables.effect: MASQUE (cf-connect-ip) over QUIC/HTTP-3
variables.notes: Exclusive group: --masque | --wg | --gool | --mim | --protocol -> one env var AETHER_PROTOCOL; later flag wins.

variables.name: AETHER_PROTOCOL=wg
variables.effect: classic WireGuard (WARP)

variables.name: AETHER_PROTOCOL=gool
variables.effect: WireGuard-in-MASQUE (gool); inner WG identity <config>-gool.toml

variables.name: AETHER_GOOL_INNER
variables.default: the one its registration names, port 2408
variables.effect: the WireGuard endpoint gool dials inside the tunnel; also selects --gool

variables.name: AETHER_GOOL_MODE=classic
variables.effect: the older gool: WireGuard tunneled in WireGuard

variables.name: AETHER_PROTOCOL=mim
variables.effect: MASQUE-in-MASQUE: two MASQUE hops on the same carrier (h3-in-h3, or h2-in-h2 with --h2)

variables.name: AETHER_MIM_OUTER_PEER
variables.effect: pin the outer MASQUE-in-MASQUE hop

variables.name: AETHER_MIM_INNER_PEER
variables.effect: pin the inner MASQUE-in-MASQUE hop

variables.name: AETHER_MIM_PEERS
variables.effect: both mim hops in one value

variables.name: AETHER_MIM_PEERS=auto
variables.effect: scan for the outer mim hop, ignoring the environment

variables.name: AETHER_PROTOCOL
variables.effect: protocol selector in one value
variables.notes: Selection precedence: AETHER_PROTOCOL > pinned wiw endpoints > pinned mim endpoints > AETHER_PEER/AETHER_WG_PEER present > interactive prompt (select_protocol lib.rs L3281).

variables.name: AETHER_SCAN
variables.effect: scan mode selector

variables.name: AETHER_SCAN=turbo
variables.effect: stop at the first candidate that answers

variables.name: AETHER_SCAN=balanced
variables.effect: default: collect a few, keep the fastest

variables.name: AETHER_SCAN=thorough
variables.effect: sweep whole ranges, for when everything looks blocked

variables.name: AETHER_SCAN=verified
variables.effect: dial only edges measured to answer connect-ip; on gool/mim keeps the two hops in separate ranges (this is what moves the exit address)

variables.name: AETHER_SCAN=ironclad
variables.effect: open a real tunnel and make a real HTTP request per candidate before trusting it

variables.name: AETHER_NOIZE
variables.default: firewall for MASQUE; balanced for WireGuard/gool
variables.effect: obfuscation/padding profile (aethernoize)

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_HTTP2=1
variables.effect: use the HTTP/2 (TCP) MASQUE carrier instead of HTTP/3 (QUIC)
variables.notes: Required with an HTTP CONNECT --upstream. Forced to 1 by --tor-reverse and --psiphon-reverse (lib.rs L216, L242).

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_HTTP2=0
variables.effect: HTTP/3 (QUIC) without asking

variables.name: AETHER_QUIC_V2=0
variables.effect: do not send the QUIC v2 version-negotiation opener (which opens HTTP/3 where v1 is blocked but v2 passes)

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_H2_PEER
variables.effect: override the peer used for the HTTP/2 transport

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_SNI
variables.effect: server name in the MASQUE ClientHello (h3 and h2); the HTTP :authority stays cloudflareaccess.com; with --ech it is the name inside the encrypted ClientHello
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L668; consts.rs L15; quic.rs L811; lib.rs L105
variables.notes: The WARP client sends consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com; aether defaults to www.cloudflare.com. Must be a domain, not an IP.

variables.name: AETHER_ECH
variables.effect: Encrypted Client Hello on MASQUE handshakes and WARP API calls; without a usable key neither goes ahead (never sends the name in the clear)
variables.notes: WireGuard has no TLS handshake, so ECH applies to MASQUE (and the API calls) only.

variables.name: AETHER_ECH_DNS
variables.accepted_values: udp://ip[:port] | tcp://ip[:port] | https://host/path with optional @address=<ip|name> and @sni=<name>; default ports 53 / 443
variables.effect: resolver --ech auto asks for the key

variables.name: AETHER_ECH_DOMAIN
variables.effect: domain whose key --ech auto takes

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_NO_DATA_CHECK=1
variables.effect: skip end-to-end data-plane validation
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L672-675; quic.rs L89; masque_h2.rs L105

variables.name: AETHER_WG_NO_DATA_CHECK=1
variables.effect: skip end-to-end data-plane validation
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L672-675; quic.rs L89; masque_h2.rs L105

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_VALIDATE_SECS
variables.effect: seconds to wait for data-plane validation
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L676-680; quic.rs L79; lib.rs L2697

variables.name: AETHER_WG_VALIDATE_SECS
variables.effect: seconds to wait for data-plane validation
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L676-680; quic.rs L79; lib.rs L2697

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_STARTUP_SECS
variables.effect: total MASQUE startup deadline

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_RECONNECT_SECS
variables.effect: delay before reconnecting after a tunnel drop (per side)

variables.name: AETHER_WG_RECONNECT_SECS
variables.effect: delay before reconnecting after a tunnel drop (per side)

variables.name: AETHER_DNS
variables.effect: resolvers used INSIDE the tunnel (domain-target SOCKS requests, incl. SOCKS5 UDP datagrams addressed by name)

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_H2_FRAGMENT=1
variables.effect: fragment the TLS ClientHello on the h2 transport and on WARP API calls (helps where a firewall resets ClientHellos ending in cloudflareclient.com)

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_H2_FRAGMENT_SIZE
variables.effect: ClientHello fragment chunk size

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_H2_FRAGMENT_DELAY
variables.effect: delay between ClientHello fragments

variables.name: AETHER_WG_KEEPALIVE
variables.effect: WireGuard persistent keepalive interval

variables.name: AETHER_WG_NO_PROFILE_RETRY
variables.effect: do not retry other obfuscation profiles during the WireGuard scan

variables.name: AETHER_CONFIG
variables.effect: base identity config path
variables.notes: Derived paths: aether-masque.toml, <config>-secondary.toml, <config>-gool.toml, <config>-lastconn.toml, <config>-tor/, <config>-psiphon/, aether-team-<name>.toml. Identity files hold private keys, mode 0600.

variables.name: AETHER_WG_CONFIG
variables.effect: identity config path for WireGuard

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_CONFIG
variables.effect: identity config path for MASQUE

variables.name: AETHER_REGISTER
variables.effect: register identities and exit (no scan, no tunnel); an identity file already there is kept, never replaced

variables.name: AETHER_API_ADDRESS
variables.accepted_values: ip or name, optional :port, IPv6 in brackets
variables.effect: where the WARP API calls go; with --mark and no --upstream an IP address only

variables.name: AETHER_API_SNI
variables.effect: server name of the WARP API ClientHello

variables.name: AETHER_API_HOST
variables.effect: HTTP host of the WARP API calls; the name the API answers by is remembered for the run
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L701; account.rs L481; consts.rs L3-7

variables.name: AETHER_TEAM
variables.effect: enrol into a Zero Trust organization (aether-team-<name>.toml; TLS pin verification on by default)
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L703; zerotrust.rs L28; tls.rs L953

variables.name: AETHER_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID
variables.effect: service-token client id for headless Zero Trust enrolment

variables.name: AETHER_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET
variables.effect: service-token client secret

variables.name: AETHER_ACCESS_TOKEN
variables.effect: an enrolment token obtained at https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/warp

variables.name: AETHER_ACCESS_EMAIL
variables.effect: sign in with a one-time code emailed to this address (interactive)

variables.name: AETHER_GATEWAY
variables.effect: send http/https through the organization gateway proxy inside the tunnel (adds a hop, enables org filtering/logging)
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L708; lib.rs L906; socks.rs L42-108

variables.name: AETHER_ROUTE_BLOCK
variables.accepted_values: comma/newline separated: domain | full:domain | keyword:x | regexp:^... | cidr-or-ip | port:n[-m] | private
variables.effect: refuse matching destinations outright (checked first); applies to TCP and UDP; behind a tun, names are recovered from TLS SNI / HTTP Host of the first bytes (AETHER_ROUTE_SNIFF)
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L710; routing.rs L187; socks.rs L786-794

variables.name: AETHER_ROUTE_DIRECT
variables.effect: send matching destinations out of the real interface, bypassing the tunnel (direct sockets carry the SO_MARK)
variables.notes: Direct loopback targets are refused for non-local clients (socks.rs L1413-1419).

variables.name: AETHER_ROUTES_FILE
variables.effect: load both routing lists from a file

variables.name: AETHER_TLS_CIPHERS
variables.effect: TLS 1.2 cipher suites appended after the TLS 1.3 ones; HTTP/3 offers none (QUIC is TLS 1.3 only)

variables.name: AETHER_TLS13_CIPHERS
variables.default: Chrome's order (AES-GCM first with AES-NI, else ChaCha20 first)
variables.effect: TLS 1.3 cipher suites in order

variables.name: AETHER_TLS_GROUPS
variables.effect: TLS groups in order

variables.name: AETHER_TLS_KEY_SHARES
variables.default: Chrome's: first group + first of the other kind (post-quantum or not)
variables.effect: groups that get a key share, in order

variables.name: AETHER_DISABLE_GREASE
variables.effect: leave out GREASE (RFC 8701) values

variables.name: AETHER_ENABLE_GREASE_SIGALGS
variables.effect: GREASE value first among signature algorithms (as Chrome does)

variables.name: AETHER_TLS_SIGALGS
variables.effect: signature algorithms in order

variables.name: AETHER_TLS_CERT_COMPRESSION
variables.effect: certificate compression offered (sent compressed certs are decompressed)

variables.name: AETHER_TLS_ALPS
variables.effect: offer ALPS under codepoint 0x44cd (new) or 0x4469 (old, Chrome 120)

variables.name: AETHER_TLS_TRUST_ANCHORS
variables.effect: trust anchor IDs asked for

variables.name: AETHER_TLS_SERVER_PADDING
variables.effect: bytes of padding asked of the server (Chrome asks 6000)

variables.name: AETHER_ENABLE_ECH_GREASE
variables.effect: send a GREASE ECH extension when no ECH key is offered

variables.name: AETHER_DISABLE_OCSP_STAPLING
variables.effect: leave out status_request

variables.name: AETHER_DISABLE_SCT
variables.effect: leave out signed_certificate_timestamp

variables.name: AETHER_DISABLE_SESSION_TICKET
variables.effect: leave out session_ticket

variables.name: AETHER_DISABLE_EXTENSION_PERMUTATION
variables.effect: keep BoringSSL's fixed extension order instead of Chrome's per-handshake permutation

variables.name: AETHER_TLS_VERIFY
variables.effect: hold the MASQUE gateway certificate to aether's SPKI pins (consts.rs MASQUE_PINS)
variables.notes: AETHER_TLS_VERIFY=0 turns it off even with --team.

variables.name: AETHER_TOR=chain
variables.effect: carry Tor inside the tunnel (aether -> warp -> tor -> internet); usual proxy keeps the warp exit, second proxy on --tor-bind

variables.name: AETHER_TOR=reverse
variables.effect: dial the tunnel through Tor (warp reached from a tor exit); forces masque over http/2 and gool's outer hop

variables.name: AETHER_TOR=only
variables.effect: no tunnel; --bind serves plain Tor; UDP ASSOCIATE is answered but only DNS (port 53) is carried, over TCP
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L586; lib.rs L131-134; socks.rs L1084-1093

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_BRIDGES (append, ';'-separated)
variables.accepted_values: bridge line, e.g. "obfs4 1.2.3.4:443 FINGERPRINT cert=... iat-mode=0"
variables.effect: add a bridge line of your own

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_BRIDGES=auto
variables.effect: go to bridges at once without trying tor plainly first

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_BRIDGE_FILE
variables.accepted_values: file of bridge lines (torrc shape; blank lines and # skipped)
variables.effect: read bridges from a file

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_RELAYS
variables.effect: running tor relays from onionoo used as plain bridges

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_RELAY_PORTS
variables.effect: which relay ports to consider (tor's own well-known ports always skipped)

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_BRIDGES=off
variables.effect: never use bridges

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_PT (append)
variables.effect: the pluggable transport binary a bridge needs

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_PT_DIR (append)
variables.effect: another folder to look in for PT binaries

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_BIND
variables.effect: where the tor-exit proxy listens with --tor and --tor-reverse

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_HTTP
variables.effect: also serve tor as an http CONNECT proxy

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_DIR
variables.effect: where tor keeps its directory cache and state

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON=chain
variables.effect: carry psiphon inside the tunnel, served on --psiphon-bind
variables.notes: Requires the psiphon-tunnel-core binary (next to aether, ./pt, PATH, or --psiphon-bin). Official release archives bundle pt/psiphon-tunnel-core and pt/lyrebird (verified in the v2.4.0 linux-x86_64 tarball).

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON=reverse
variables.effect: dial the tunnel through psiphon (TCP only -> forces h2, refuses --wg/--gool-classic)

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON=only
variables.effect: no tunnel; --bind serves plain psiphon; UDP ASSOCIATE answered but only DNS carried, over TCP
variables.consuming_code: aether/src/cli.rs L600; lib.rs L136-139; socks.rs L1084-1093

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_CONFIG
variables.effect: overlay a psiphon config of your own

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_BIND
variables.effect: where the psiphon proxy listens with --psiphon and --psiphon-reverse

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_HTTP
variables.effect: also serve psiphon as an http CONNECT proxy

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_REGION
variables.effect: ask psiphon to leave from this country (log lists AvailableEgressRegions)

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_MODE
variables.effect: cdn = only fronted meek through a CDN; direct = no fronting

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_CDN_IPS
variables.effect: addresses to try as CDN fronting edges

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_CDN_SNI
variables.effect: server names to present to those edges

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_CDN_SETS
variables.accepted_values: cloudflare, fastly, cloudfront, psiphon-akamai, psiphon-bunny, vercel, github, curated-fronting, legacy-android-overrides
variables.effect: which built-in edge lists the fronting scan tries (after --psiphon-cdn-ips)

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_DIR
variables.effect: where psiphon keeps its data

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_BIN
variables.effect: the psiphon-tunnel-core binary to run

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_SERVER_ENTRIES
variables.accepted_values: file of server entries (remote-list unpacked form)
variables.effect: server entries psiphon starts with (first connection need not download the list; fetched list merged on top)

variables.name: AETHER_PERF_PROFILE
variables.effect: force a resource profile (low: routers/small boards; medium: desktop; high: servers); also sets the SOCKS client-limit tier

variables.name: AETHER_LOG_LEVEL
variables.effect: log verbosity (RUST_LOG overrides)

variables.name: AETHER_LOG_LEVEL=debug
variables.effect: shortcut for --log-level debug

variables.name: AETHER_PSIPHON_READY_SECS
variables.effect: how long to wait for psiphon to tunnel

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_DIRECT_SECS
variables.effect: how long to try tor plainly before bridges

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_STALL_SECS
variables.effect: give up on a bridge after this long with no headway

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_BRIDGE_SECS
variables.effect: the longest any one bridge may take

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_COUNTRY
variables.effect: ask bridgedb for bridges in this country

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_CHECK
variables.effect: endpoint tor must reach before it counts as working

variables.name: AETHER_TOR_LOG
variables.effect: how loud tor's own logging is

variables.name: AETHER_ROUTE_SNIFF
variables.effect: read the server name (TLS SNI / HTTP Host) from a connection's first bytes so domain routing rules work behind a tun front end
variables.notes: This is exactly the mechanism that makes --route-block/--route-direct name rules effective for zeptun-originated IP connections.

variables.name: AETHER_ROUTE_SNIFF_MS
variables.effect: how long to wait for those first bytes before deciding on address/port rules alone

variables.name: AETHER_WG_ENDPOINT_COOLDOWN_SECS
variables.effect: how long an endpoint is left out of rescans after its tunnel ended twice in a row within five minutes of starting

variables.name: AETHER_WG_STALE_SECS
variables.effect: silence on a wireguard tunnel before it counts as dead
variables.verification: documented+listed in help; exact consumer line not independently re-verified

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_H2_KEEPALIVE_SECS
variables.effect: HTTP/2 carrier keepalive interval

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_H2_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_SECS
variables.effect: how long an h2 keepalive may go unanswered

variables.name: AETHER_IRONCLAD_PORT
variables.effect: port the ironclad scan's real HTTP request goes to

variables.name: AETHER_MAX_CLIENTS
variables.default: 512 (Low) / 2048 (Medium) / 8192 (High) by resource tier, clamped by the open-file limit
variables.effect: proxy clients served at once; past it new ones wait for a free slot

variables.name: AETHER_HALF_CLOSE_SECS
variables.effect: how long a half-closed client connection may sit silent before closing

variables.name: AETHER_TCP_KEEPALIVE_SECS
variables.effect: idle time before a tunnel TCP keepalive; three unanswered close the connection

variables.name: AETHER_TCP_CONNECT_SECS
variables.effect: how long a connection through the tunnel may take to open

variables.name: AETHER_REPROVISION
variables.effect: 0 = report a Cloudflare-refused identity instead of silently registering a fresh one

variables.name: RUST_LOG
variables.effect: overrides --log-level as the env_logger filter

variables.name: AETHER_MASQUE_MTU
